newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Crackdown urged on S.African govt money misuse.
newsitem.headline: Crackdown urged on S.African govt money misuse.

text.p: Troubled by growing signs of public service corruption and financial mismanagement, South Africa is considering tougher action against wrongdoers.

Representatives of national and provincial government public accounts committees met on Thursday to start mapping out how they could help clean up government financial management and clamp down on unauthorised expenditure which has led to a string of scandals over the last year.
These have ranged from the unauthorised use of money for an AIDS awareness programme, housing projects and alleged high living by members of the controversial Independent Broadcasting Authority.
"One cannot over-estimate the importance of your task," parliamentary speaker Frene Ginwala told the Association of Public Accounts Committees.
"Corruption and mismanagement undermine democracy and everything that we have fought and struggled for."
Commissions of inquiry have been appointed in several provinces to examine local scandals and some delegates asked what role this left for public accounts committees.
Deputy Auditor General Bertie Loots said that it was clear tougher action had to be taken against wayward civil servants.
He suggested that this could include reprimands, non-renewal of contracts and fines.
Unauthorised expenditure did not necessarily mean money had been wasted, misused or stolen but did point to weak financial controls which could also lead to fraud and corruption, he said.

Ginwala pledged to use aid funds, mainly from the European Union, to help strengthen public accounts committees, who complained that they did not have enough researchers or technical expertise to investigate some cases.
